added_models.model: Human anti-CD19 CAR T cells (CTL019) against MCL cell lines and primary MCL cells, in vitro and in NSG mouse MCL xenografts

efficacy.model: Human anti-CD19 CAR T cells (CTL019) against MCL cell lines and primary MCL cells, in vitro and in NSG mouse MCL xenografts
efficacy.note: CTL019 monotherapy controlled xenografted MCL better than ibrutinib, though most mice later relapsed; no MCL patient data yet.
efficacy.quote: In a xenograft MCL model, we showed superior disease control in the CTL019- as compared with ibrutinib-treated mice (median survival not reached vs. 95 days, P < 0.005) but most mice receiving CTL019 monotherapy eventually relapsed.

efficacy.model: Human anti-CD19 CAR T cells (CTL019) against MCL cell lines and primary MCL cells, in vitro and in NSG mouse MCL xenografts
efficacy.note: ZUMA-2: 93% objective response after brexucabtagene in MCL, as the MCL xenograft predicted for a sibling CD19 CAR.
efficacy.quote: The primary efficacy analysis showed that 93% (95% confidence interval [CI], 84 to 98) of the 60 patients in the primary efficacy analysis had an objective response; 67% (95% CI, 53 to 78) had a complete response.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. Registry NCT02601313 results first posted 2020-09-10; NEJM online 2020-04.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: model used CTL019 (4-1BB) not the CD28 brexucabtagene construct, so product_in_model false; direction held. Relapse after monotherapy in mice not scored against ZUMA-2 durability.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: xenograft MCL disease control vs IRRC ORR 93% (CR 67%)

added_models.model: KTE-X19 CAR T cells co-cultured with CD19+ tumour cell lines in vitro (cytotoxicity, cytokine release, proliferation)

efficacy.model: KTE-X19 CAR T cells co-cultured with CD19+ tumour cell lines in vitro (cytotoxicity, cytokine release, proliferation)
efficacy.note: The product itself killed CD19+ tumour lines in co-culture; filed in the BLA as primary pharmacology before ZUMA-2 results.
efficacy.short: KTE-X19 killed CD19+ lines in vitro
efficacy.quote: In vitro characterization of KTE-X19 included demonstration of CD19-dependent cytotoxicity, cytokine release, and proliferation when co-cultured with tumor cell lines expressing CD19.
efficacy.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy: ZUMA-2 (NCT02601313) first posted 2015; the in vitro characterization preceded dosing but was first public in the SBRA (2020-07-23). Cell lines not named.

efficacy.model: KTE-X19 CAR T cells co-cultured with CD19+ tumour cell lines in vitro (cytotoxicity, cytokine release, proliferation)
efficacy.note: ZUMA-2: 93% objective response after brexucabtagene in MCL, consistent with CD19-dependent killing in co-culture.
efficacy.quote: The primary efficacy analysis showed that 93% (95% confidence interval [CI], 84 to 98) of the 60 patients in the primary efficacy analysis had an objective response; 67% (95% CI, 53 to 78) had a complete response.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (NEJM). SBRA states the in vitro data but not alongside ZUMA-2 efficacy; registry results posted 2020-09-10.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: SBRA lists the co-culture in the same document as ZUMA-2 but does not compare them; the target lines are unnamed and may not be MCL. Cytokine release in vitro not scored as a CRS prediction.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: in vitro CD19-dependent cytotoxicity vs IRRC ORR 93% (CR 67%)

considered_not_added: Loncastuximab in vitro cytotoxicity on the GRANTA-519 MCL line (BLA 761196 review, Zammarchi 2018): an MCL model, but the only MCL patient data (LOTIS-1, n=15) have ORR as a secondary endpoint (primary = DLT/safety), so no admissible efficacy comparison; would be untested/unsettled only
